content.text: Most tutorials about building a digital store focus on the storefront. The storefront is the last thing you should configure. The backend is what makes the store work — and the backend is what most creators get wrong when they try to build without a clear sequence. In Stack 01, Google Apps Script serves as the backend Web App — it receives the NOW[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-payment-options-ethiopian-digital-creators-works-how|payment]]s webhook, validates the signature, confirms the transaction on-chain, logs the order to Google Sheets, and sends the delivery email via Gmail. In Stack 02, Cloudflare Workers replaces Apps Script with a faster, more scalable serverless backend that integrates natively with Supabase for order storage and Resend for email delivery. Configure the backend first, set the webhook endpoint URL in NOWPayments second, build the storefront third, and test on mainnet fourth.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The key to a successful online store lies in its infrastructure. Traditional platforms often restrict access based on geographical location or impose stringent requirements. In contrast, a sovereign commerce infrastructure, such as the one provided by COREMERCH, offers a reliable and unrestricted way to sell digital products. By leveraging GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, or similar services for hosting, and integrating with crypto payment processors like NOWPayments, creators can bypass conventional platforms' limitations.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-deploying-digital-store-cloudflare-pages-free-works-25|How Deploying]] your crypto store, you need a clear [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/understanding-bitcoin-payments-digital-downloads-plain-language-infrastructure-18|COREMERCH guide to understanding]] of your product offerings, target audience, and the technical requirements for your store. This includes selecting the right hosting service, configuring your backend logic, and setting up your payment and delivery pipelines. It's also crucial to choose a crypto payment processor that supports a wide range of cryptocurrencies and has a low transaction fee, such as NOWPayments.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Setting up your payment pipeline involves integrating your store with a crypto payment processor. NOWPayments supports over 300 cryptocurrencies and charges a minimal fee of 0.5%. For delivery, you can use services like Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 to store and distribute your digital products securely. Ensuring a seamless and automated process for both payment and delivery is vital for a positive customer experience.
Empower your digital sales with a sovereign commerce infrastructure.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once your store is set up, going live is straightforward. You'll need to configure your domain, test your payment and delivery pipelines, and ensure that your store is accessible to your target audience. Processing your first transaction is a milestone, confirming that your infrastructure is working as intended. It's essential to monitor your store's performance and be ready to scale as your business grows.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Scaling your crypto store involves increasing your product offerings, enhancing your marketing efforts, and possibly expanding your technical infrastructure to handle higher traffic and sales volumes. This might include upgrading your hosting plan, optimizing your backend logic for better performance, and exploring more advanced features of your payment and delivery services. A well-planned scaling strategy ensures that your store remains efficient and profitable as it grows.

The difference between Stack 01 and Stack 02 is not which one works — both work — it is which one fits your situation. Stack 01 is the right choice if you want to deploy yourself, you are comfortable with Google Workspace tools, and your initial volume is under 100 orders per day. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 documents the complete Stack 01 build with full source code and step-by-step configuration. Stack 02 is the right choice if you want the deployment done for you, you need higher volume capacity, or you want email deliverability infrastructure configured from day one. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 has COREMERCH deploy Stack 02 under your accounts in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff. Both are available at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Bypass conventional payment platforms' restrictions with crypto.

For creators seeking a hassle-free and efficient way to establish their online stores, the Edge Commerce Stack provides a ready-to-deploy solution. This stack, priced at $197, includes all the necessary components for a fully operational store, from hosting to payment processing, ensuring a seamless and secure customer experience.
Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy your crypto store, follow these steps: select your hosting service, set up your backend logic, integrate with a crypto payment processor, configure your payment and delivery pipelines, test your store, and go live. Ensure you monitor your store's performance and have a plan in place for scaling as your business grows. Utilizing the Edge Commerce Stack can streamline this process, providing a solid foundation for your online store.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the primary benefit of using a sovereign commerce infrastructure?
The primary benefit is the ability to sell digital products without relying on conventional restricted platforms like Stripe or PayPal.
How do I choose the right crypto payment processor?
Look for processors that support a wide range of cryptocurrencies and have low transaction fees, such as NOWPayments.
What is the role of backend logic in my crypto store?
Backend logic, configured with services like Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, automates tasks such as order processing and product delivery.
Can I use my existing domain with the Edge Commerce Stack?
Yes, the Edge Commerce Stack allows you to configure your domain, ensuring a professional and recognizable presence for your online store.
How does the Edge Commerce Stack support scaling?
The stack is designed to be scalable, with components like Supabase for order storage and Cloudflare Pages for hosting, which can handle increased traffic and sales volumes.
